Lutsk Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Volynska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. This is Lutsk's Old Jewish cemetery, existing since at least the 16th century — an expedition led by S. An-sky in the early 20th century recorded a tombstone dating to 1662. It included a Karaite section, overbuilt in the late 19th century; the local community, alongside others, represented Volyn in the Council of Four Lands. Among its most notable religious figures were Rabbi Shlomo of Lutsk, a disciple of the Maggid of Mezritch and one of the first editors of Hasidic literature, and Yoel Halperin, known as Yoel the Great or Yoel Baal Shem. The Jewish population reached its peak of 24,398 in 1912, supported by 50 synagogues and dominant local trade and industry by the interwar period; following the June 1941 Nazi occupation, 5,000 Jews were murdered immediately, and the ghetto's September 1942 liquidation claimed 25,000 more.
